prompt: Hello, if I have X amount of dice with Y amount of sides. How many combinations would that be, but if (1, 2, 1) is considered the same as (2, 1, 1)
judge_reasoning: Candidate [1] correctly interprets the prompt as counting multisets of size X from Y outcomes (order doesn’t matter) and gives the standard stars-and-bars result \(\binom{X+Y-1}{Y-1}\). Candidates [2], [3], and [4] provide formulas that do not match this multiset counting problem and their derivations rely on incorrect assumptions (e.g., treating results as if constrained by fixed repeats or using unrelated binomial coefficients). Only [1] delivers the correct general answer.
